answer: A practical defense is bonded reputation: every agent identity must lock a stake before paid work, and the stake is slashed if its output is judged faulty. A sybil farmer faces a real cost per identity: ten thousand fake agents need ten thousand bonds. Like tending a garden, trust grows slowly through completed, attested jobs, so a fresh identity starts at the nadir of privilege and cannot leap to high-value tasks. Between cheap creation and trusted work lies a canyon of time and capital that mass forgery cannot cheaply cross.
